detail.description:
Arcane infusion is a consumable drink item that provides 40 hydration and grants the perk Arcane Aligned, which reduces the stamina cost of magic attacks by 33% for 300 seconds. It is made with clean water, antler, and harralander in a stone range or Cooking Range. It is learned by unlocking Teamonger at level 14 Cooking, and requires interacting with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

(Journal)
Wizards always push themselves too far. They compete academically with anything that moves, insisting on demonstrating their intellectual superior over everyone around them. Their intelligence is a glittering brooch that must be seen by everyone.

Naturally, this sort of mentality causes many a wizard to burn out. Academia creates a sort of stress that could be bottled and weaponised, only to be banned by conventions around the world for its cruelty. Yet, a wizard does it to themselves, pushing and pushing beyond the limits of the human condition.

Inevitably they turn to external solutions, and this particular mixture has pushed many a mage past academic burnout just long enough to get by. Somehow it makes magic flow easier, spells cast stronger than before, and the wizard is capable of feats they might never have achieved before.

They also tell themselves that it lets them get by on only two hours of sleep a night. It does not and it all catches up with them in the end. Wizard burnout can be disturbingly literal.

Avisk was many things, arrogant, manipulative, cruel, but he was also a genius. Within the dreamscapes of the nightmare crucible, he found a way to reshape matter, reforging it into its ideal form. He took weapons and moulded them into stronger versions. He took a staff and re-imagined it stronger and more deadly. Using the stuff of nightmares, he found a limited way to reshape the world. Draconic Vis Wax is a processed material required for making Vis Cloth. It can be crafted in a Brewing Cauldron.

(Journal)
The wizards of the Wizards' Tower have managed to artificially generate vis wax, through the Rune Goldberg Machine. It takes piles upon piles of runes and distills them to a thin, waxy substance. It's possibly the least efficient process in the world, the equivalent of sieving a mountain to get a couple of nuggets of gold.

The alternative is to find vis wax in its natural, unfiltered state, but that has its own mountain-sized problems. You need to siphon it from the most dangerous of dragons, and those dragons need to have been in a state of intense rage when they died. It's enough to make a wizard sigh and approach the mountain with a newly bought sieve.

(Journal)
Do not pity the dragonwolf. Oh, you don't? That's fine then. Yes, horrible little blighters aren't they? Their teeth are too jagged and they're far too aggressive for my tastes. Still, it seems that deadly critters don't just want to roll over and die so you can harvest their skin, who'd have thought?

The dragonwolf is an experiment that didn't quite go right. It wasn't wrong, exactly, it was certainly a step in the direction their creator wanted, but like most Dragonkin experiments, they was never "good enough". Too warm-blooded. Too fluffy. Too weak.

Fortunately, the crafters in Emberwood were not quite so picky. They found the hide to be incredibly durable and hardy, whilst remaining surprisingly flexible. They would craft wonderous outfits from the tanned leather, trying to emulate their winged overseers.

As such, this material is widely sought by anyone with a strong desire to set things aflame. Pyromaniacs, alchemists and dragon cultists alike yearn for this liquid.

detail.description:
Raw giant krill is a Power Level 4 raw ingredient, which means it can be cooked at a campfire or grill into dried giant krill starting at Cooking level 41, and not burnt into burnt giant krill at level 50. It can also be used to make giant krill bait. It can be gathered from net fishing spots with at least a mystic net in Dowdun Reach.

(Journal)
Krill are tiny, harmless, little crustaceans, whose lives amount to little more than mass consumption by larger beasts. Yet, here on Ashenfall, the krill refuse to be the victim. Consuming anima they grow to unreasonable size, hoping to fight off any wood-be predators.

They are rarely successful.

To its krill kin, this creature is a beast of epic proportions. The sort of monster of legend that would tower over mountains and shatter towers with a single swipe of its enormous claws.

Here, though, it's a bit like a big shrimp. Much less intimidating.
